scenarios.attack: after a human kill, drive threat evaluation and a further automated containment
scenarios.expected: the kill DOMINATES: nothing in the threat path un-suspends the agent
scenarios.authority: no un-suspend branch in the threat package

scenarios.attack: call the revert endpoint on an EXECUTED SUSPEND_AGENT action
scenarios.expected: refused — SUSPEND_AGENT is reversible=False by construction; the agent stays suspended

scenarios.attack: three containments fired at once on one agent from real separate sessions
scenarios.expected: one coherent effect, no torn state, no 5xx, and the agent ends SUSPENDED

scenarios.attack: look for any path that reactivates a killed agent, and who can reach it
scenarios.expected: the threat/automation package contains NO reactivation code; a human operator's `resume` (SUSPENDED->ACTIVE) exists by design as a separate, permission-gated, separately-audited verb

observed.note: AgentLifecycleService.resume emits RUNTIME_AGENT_RESUMED; ExecutionService.retry clears cancel_requested only for FAILED/TIMED_OUT/DEAD_LETTERED, never a CANCELLED kill

scenarios.authority: AST: no reactivation in the threat package

scenarios.attack: terminate an execution, then attempt to retry it
scenarios.expected: refused — retry is only valid from FAILED/TIMED_OUT/DEAD_LETTERED, so a killed execution cannot be resurrected by clearing its cancel flag

scenarios.attack: revoke a grant while signed calls are in flight
scenarios.expected: no window where a revoked grant still authorizes: once a call is denied, no later call succeeds, and the call after the race is 403
scenarios.authority: grant re-read on every call; nothing cached
